clue.text: Parts sent for repair, wings

indicators.note: something sent for repair gets taken apart and put back together, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter as raw material

explanation.surface: Damaged aircraft parts, namely the wings, are dispatched to a workshop to be mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wings' suggests aircraft, but the wings meant are those of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Transepts are the arms of a cross-shaped church, projecting either side of the nave like wings from a body.

clue.text: Emaciated, though not in chopper

indicators.note: 'not in' tells you the two letters spelling 'in' are to be dropped from the phrase

blocks.note: emaciated means far too thin, written as two words

explanation.surface: Someone is gaunt, though not when they are in a helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: TOO THIN loses IN to leave TOOTH. 'Chopper' looks like a helicopter or axe; here it is slang for a tooth, since teeth chop food.
explanation.definitionFit: Choppers is informal slang for teeth, the things that bite and cut food, so a single one is a chopper.

clue.text: Can I get in trouble stimulating response?

indicators.note: being in trouble means being in a mess, so the preceding letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the three words used letter for letter
taken as written; it also starts the indicator phrase

explanation.surface: A worried person asks whether a provocative remark will land them in hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' does double duty, supplying letters and forming part of 'in trouble'. The surface 'response' sounds like a reaction to a remark, but it is the body's immune response.
explanation.definitionFit: An antigen is a substance that provokes the immune system into producing antibodies, so antigenic means triggering that bodily reaction.

clue.text: See 8

blocks.note: surface reading: a pointer sending the solver to another clue
setter's reading: this light holds the second word of the two-word food clued at 8 down, its letters the tail of that clue's wordplay

explanation.definitionFit: The answer completes the phrase at 8 down, the snack Paddington Bear carries, so its meaning lives in that clue.

clue.text: Pius perhaps to yield, oddly amazed

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the odd-numbered positions of the next word, first, third and fifth

blocks.note: several popes took the name Pius, so Pius is an example of the title
letters one, three and five of yield

explanation.surface: A pontiff is pressed to give way and is astonished at the demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pop-eyed has eyes bulging wide open, the classic look of a person astonished or staring in disbelief.

clue.text: All entertained by a student union climbing in here in. . .

definitions.note: runs on into 6 down: a place here in Peru

indicators.note: to be entertained by a host is to be inside their house, so the first word goes inside the union
in a down light climbing means rising up the column, so the assembled letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: taken as written
the National Union of Students, the UK students' body
taken as written, placed inside the union

explanation.surface: Everyone is hosted by a student group that goes climbing somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: A + N(ALL)US gives ANALLUS, which read upwards is SULLANA, a city in northern Peru. The ellipsis carries the clue on into 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullana is a city in the north-west of Peru, so it is a place found there, the country named in the next clue.

clue.text: Redhead featured in lyric for the introduction

indicators.note: something featured in a piece appears inside it, so one letter sits within the other word

blocks.note: a lyric is a short poem
the head, or first letter, of red

explanation.surface: A red-haired person gets a mention in a song's words as an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' reads as a ginger person but means the first letter of red.
explanation.definitionFit: A proem is a formal word for a preface or preamble, the opening section that introduces a book or speech.

clue.text: . . .the country for sport in general and one specifically

blocks.note: physical education, school sport of every kind
rugby union, one particular sport

explanation.surface: A nation is known for sport broadly and for one game in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) is sport in general; RU (rugby union) is one sport specifically. The leading dots pick up from 5 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a South American nation, so it is a country, the one where the city in the previous clue lies.

clue.text: Daggers: Swedish chemist decapitated by one

indicators.note: having the head cut off means losing the first letter of the name

blocks.note: Alfred Nobel, Swedish chemist and inventor of dynamite, minus his first letter
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a Swedish scientist beheaded by a single dagger-wielder.
explanation.walkthrough: NOBEL loses N; 'by' simply places I next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing an obelus is the dagger mark used for footnotes, and obeli is its plural, so they are typographical daggers.

clue.text: (and 3) Treks around the country taking in Andes, organised for deaf primarily, then fare to...

definitions.note: with 3 down, and running on into 13 down: the food Paddington Bear carries

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so the mountain letters plus the extra one are set in a new order
primarily asks for only the first letter of the preceding word
around says the walking word wraps the rest, which goes inside it
a country taking in something holds it within its borders, so it encloses the next letters

blocks.note: treks are marches; only the first three letters fall in this light, the tail ends 3 down
the African country Malawi; its last two letters fall in 3 down
the South American range, shuffled; one letter lands here and the other four start 3 down
the first letter of deaf

explanation.surface: A rambling account of a journey: hikes across a nation including the Andes, planned for deaf travellers, then onward.
explanation.walkthrough: The full build spans 8 and 3 down: MARCHES wraps MALAWI, which wraps a shuffle of ANDES plus D, giving MAR-MALA-DESAND-WI-CHES. This light takes the first nine letters; the dots lead into 13 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington Bear always keeps marmalade sandwiches under his hat, so they are the food associated with that character from Peru.

clue.text: Newspaper maintained by other one, daily perhaps

definitions.note: daily is an example of how frequent something is

indicators.note: something maintained by others is held up and kept within their care, so the paper sits inside
an other form of a word is a different version of it, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
the Financial Times, a British daily

explanation.surface: A newspaper is kept going by another publication, perhaps a daily one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper' and 'daily' look like the same idea, but daily belongs to the definition. FT, the Financial Times, is the crossword's favourite paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening daily happens frequently, so daily is one instance of the adverb meaning many times or regularly.

clue.text: Supporter cut back on consideration for 13's northern relative

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the first two words are read from right to left
one piece placed on another is added after it, so the last item follows

blocks.note: a bra is a garment that supports
to lop is to cut off
to give someone an ear is to give them consideration

explanation.surface: A backer reduces spending after a rethink about someone's northern family.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is Paddington, a bear from Peru, so his northern relative is the Arctic bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is a bear, and the white bear of the Arctic is a fellow member of that animal family living far to the north.

clue.text: On his demand, prompt delivery meant not being late

definitions.text: On his demand, prompt delivery meant not being late

blocks.note: surface reading: a punctual courier service or speedy postal round
setter's reading: a robber's victims had to hand over valuables at once to avoid being 'the late' someone, that is, dead

explanation.walkthrough: The old cry 'Stand and deliver!' was the mounted robber's demand, and 'late' means deceased as well as overdue.
explanation.definitionFit: An eighteenth-century mounted robber held up coaches on the road, demanding valuables with the threat of death if travellers refused.

clue.text: Capital of 6 down or of Mali, strangely

indicators.note: strangely suggests the African country's letters appear in an odd arrangement

blocks.note: the West African country's name, letter for letter; 'of' merely joins

explanation.surface: A query whether this is the capital of one country or of Mali in an odd sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru, the country that is the answer at 6 down.

clue.text: . . .the station, from 6 down?

definitions.note: the bear from Peru, not a phrase meaning the same

blocks.note: first meaning: the London mainline rail terminus serving the west
second meaning: Michael Bond's bear who arrived from Peru, named after where he was found

explanation.walkthrough: Read on from 8 and 3 down: the bear in Michael Bond's books was found at a London rail terminus, labelled as coming from 'darkest Peru'. The question mark marks the second sense as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The station is a London mainline terminus, and the fictional bear from Peru was named after it by the family who found him.

clue.text: People unable to return service are threatened

blocks.note: men as people in general
in tennis a player who cannot return a serve has been aced

explanation.surface: Tennis players who cannot get the ball back find themselves under threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' sounds like help or staff, but it is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: To be menaced is to be put in fear by someone's hostile intentions, the same as being intimidated or put at risk.

clue.text: Dominant woman raising the right atmosphere in contest

indicators.note: in a down light raising lifts the letters upward, so they are read from bottom to top
in says the flipped letters are placed inside the word for a contest

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
the air is the atmosphere around us
a match is a sporting contest

explanation.surface: A formidable woman lifts the mood correctly during a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is a woman who heads a family or group, the female equivalent of a patriarch with authority over it.

clue.text: Approaching a river, a desert in 6 down

blocks.note: at, as in nearly at the door, close to
taken as written
the Cam, the river through Cambridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nearing a river, a traveller reaches a desert in Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam is the Cambridge river, a favourite of setters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atacama is the very dry desert of the Pacific coast of South America, running from Chile up into southern Peru.

clue.text: Love, given 30 seconds in decline, becomes hate

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair of items inside the word for falling off

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
half a minute, and also half of the six letters of minute
to abate is to lessen or decline

explanation.surface: A cynical view: love, after half a minute of waning, turns into hate.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful 30 seconds is half a minute, and also half of the word minute. 'Love' and 'hate' look like opposites to be contrasted; love is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest intensely, so as a verb it means the same as to hate.

clue.text: Opening dismissed by those not twisting in heart

definitions.note: singular: tickers is slang for hearts

indicators.note: dismissing the opening means sending away the first letter

blocks.note: in the card game pontoon a player either twists for another card or sticks

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: an opening batsman is out to steady bowlers who keep their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon, a card game like blackjack, lets players twist (take a card) or stick (hold), so those not twisting are stickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for the heart, which ticks like a clock as it beats.

clue.text: Show a bit of leg and enjoy the party

blocks.note: the shin is the front part of the lower leg
dig is slang for like or enjoy

explanation.surface: Advice for a guest: flash some leg and have a good time at the celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a lively celebration or noisy social gathering.

clue.text: Greek character gains benefit around hot, wet pit

indicators.note: around says the benefit word wraps itself about the next letter

blocks.note: mu, the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A Greek person on welfare ends up near a steamy, soggy hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A mud hole is a hollow in the ground filled with mud or muddy water, a soggy pit.

clue.text: Dramatist wants further story penned

indicators.note: something penned is enclosed as in a pen, so the tale goes inside

blocks.note: more as in additional, further
a story can mean an untruth

explanation.surface: A playwright needs another narrative written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like writing, fitting a playwright, but signals enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the great seventeenth-century French comic playwright, author of Tartuffe and The Misanthrope.

clue.text: Ancient location of Hollywood?

blocks.note: where something is located: in a place
Hollywood lies in California, abbreviated CA

explanation.surface: Asking where old Hollywood was set.
explanation.walkthrough: Hollywood is located IN CA, the postal abbreviation for California. 'Ancient' is a noun here: a person of antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inca was a member of the ancient South American people whose empire was centred on Peru, so one of the ancients.

clue.text: 20-n capital where copper the last business

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A policeman settles in the Inca capital as its final trade.
explanation.walkthrough: '20-n' makes the answer at 20 into an adjective, Incan. 'Copper' reads as a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuzco, in the Andes of Peru, was the capital city of the Inca empire.

clue.text: Sick with boredom, turning tail, in recent year (in which it was celebrated)

definitions.note: the pronoun in the bracket refers back to the answer

indicators.note: turning the tail means the last pair of letters swap round
in says the earlier letters sit inside the year

blocks.note: ill means sick
ennui is listless boredom
2000 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Fed up with a recent anniversary year and its relentless celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket defines the answer: 2000, written MM, is when the event was celebrated. The year is the container, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The year 2000 was widely celebrated as the start of a new thousand-year period, which is the event the bracket refers to.

clue.text: Fruit of opposite halves of European capitals

indicators.note: opposite halves means the back half of one name and the front half of the other

blocks.note: the back half of Rome
the front half of London

explanation.surface: Produce from contrasting parts of Europe's great cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The cities are unstated: ROME gives its back half, ME, and LONDON its front half, LON.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large sweet fruit of the gourd family, such as a cantaloupe or watermelon.

clue.text: Exaltation of tender love

indicators.note: exaltation is lifting up, and in a down light raising letters reads them from bottom to top

blocks.note: tender as in painful to touch

explanation.surface: A rhapsody on gentle romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender love' reads as one phrase, but tender means sore here.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros was the Greek god of love, and the name is used for erotic or passionate love.

clue.text: Something to cut storm, about zero (perhaps) degrees

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible variant of the number, so its letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rage word goes around the rest

blocks.note: to storm is to rage
taken as written before rearranging
D is the abbreviation for degree

explanation.surface: Weather talk: something cuts through a storm at about freezing point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zero degrees' looks like a temperature, a false trail; the words supply letters separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A razor edge is the keen blade of a razor, an implement for shaving, and so something that cuts.

clue.text: Follow Billy literarily back to junction

indicators.note: back says the literary name is read from its end to its start
to here means attached to, so one piece is joined to the other

blocks.note: a T-junction
Billy Liar, Keith Waterhouse's novel about a fantasist

explanation.surface: A tip to track Billy, in literary fashion, back to a crossroads.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Liar is a 1959 English novel and film about a daydreaming clerk; 'literarily' signals the book.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to follow them, tracking their path from behind.

clue.text: Laughs with 20 when conspiring?

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: the word that follows 20's answer in the idiom for conspiring

blocks.note: first meaning: loud bursts of mirth
second meaning: placed after the answer at 20 it completes the phrase for being in league with someone

explanation.walkthrough: INCA followed by this answer gives 'in cahoots', meaning in league or conspiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoots are loud bursts of laughter, and the same letters finish the idiom for plotting together when set after the ancient people.

clue.text: Vegetable for the Head of Conservation?

blocks.note: green means environmentally conscious, concerned with conservation
bean is old slang for the head

explanation.surface: A vegetable suggestion for an environmental agency's chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The Head of Conservation reads as an official's title; read backwards, it is a green head.
explanation.definitionFit: A green bean is the edible pod of a bean plant, such as the French bean, eaten as a vegetable.
